theme: Saylor teases more bitcoin as Strategy's bitcoin per share slips and STRC moves to daily dividends, ETFs see outflows after the Binance hack, SpaceX's AI business now rivals Starlink with the stock at its IPO price, Cybercabs keep piling up in Texas, and the AI spending payoff is questioned while bonds price a Fed hike.

items.title: Strategy's weekly bitcoin buys and sales since Jan 2025
items.picked: Michael Saylor posted a SaylorTracker chart on Sunday morning captioned 'We found room for even more orange', the kind of post that has usually come before a Monday purchase filing. Strategy's Q3 results this week showed it bought 7,218 BTC and sold 5,552 BTC in the quarter, per its filing as reported by Cryptonews.
items.matters: After two years of buying nearly every week, Strategy has started selling some bitcoin to help fund preferred dividends and buybacks, so each new filing shows whether it is back to steady net buying.
items.know: Through Oct 12 2026 the tab has 182,697 BTC bought and 6,948 BTC sold in 2026, with 848,250 BTC held. The last four rows are small buys (950, 1,665, 334 and 250 BTC), and the sales were in Jun 1 to Aug 10. The ledger stops at Oct 12, so it misses later buys that took holdings to 848,517 BTC by Oct 25, per Strategy's Q3 release.

items.title: Strategy: bitcoin per diluted share vs share count
items.picked: A poll by BritishHodl trending on X found 61.5% of bitcoin-treasury investors care most about stock price and only 18.6% about bitcoin per share, and Strategy reported a -3.7% year-to-date BTC Yield on Oct 25, down from +4.5% in July.
items.matters: Bitcoin per share is what a shareholder actually owns, so when the share count grows faster than the bitcoin pile, holders get diluted even as the company's total holdings rise.
items.know: On Oct 12 the tab has 187,750 sats per diluted share on 451.8M assumed diluted shares, down from a peak of 220,429 sats on Jun 1 2026, when the share count was 382.8M. It was 158,827 sats in Jan 2025. The share count is the tab's own diluted estimate at each 8-K, so it won't match Strategy's reported figures exactly, and the data ends Oct 12.

items.title: Strategy's preferred stock outstanding by series (STRF, STRC, STRE, STRK, STRD)
items.picked: STRC switches to daily dividends today, with a Nov 1 record date and Nov 2 payment, after 99.3% of votes cast approved the change, per Strategy's Q3 call. Strategy also said it has bought back $2.04B of STRC.
items.matters: Preferred stock now funds much of Strategy's bitcoin buying, and its dividends are a fixed cost that has to be paid whatever bitcoin does.
items.know: On Oct 16 the tab has $13.7B of preferred outstanding at stated amounts, including $8.8B of STRC, down from a peak of $15.5B total and $10.5B of STRC on May 22 2026. STRF, STRE, STRK and STRD are flat at $1.3B, $0.9B, $1.4B and $1.4B. The data ends Oct 16 and the image is the Oct 19 export, which tops out at $13.9B.

items.title: US spot bitcoin ETF daily net flows ($ millions)
items.picked: US spot bitcoin ETFs had $643M of net outflows on Friday, Oct 30, ending a four-day inflow streak after the $6.3B Binance hack, per SoSoValue data reported by TokenPost. Binance resumed bitcoin withdrawals on Sunday after covering 95% of the stolen tokens, per Reuters.
items.matters: ETF flows are the clearest daily read on US institutional demand, and they set the tone for bitcoin going into Monday.
items.know: The tab, which uses Farside data, has -$643.2M on Oct 30 after inflows of $110.3M, $176M, $137.3M and $17.2M on Oct 26 to 29. Adding up the tab's daily figures gives net outflows of about $516M for October, against about $2.65B of inflows in September. Flows are in dollars, not bitcoin, and the image was redrawn from the tab because the Drive export stops in mid-October.

items.title: Bitcoin price relative to its 200-week average
items.picked: On Strategy's Q3 call Saylor said 'We're at the beginning of the next Bitcoin bull market' and pointed to bitcoin trading 21% above its 200-week moving average, per Cryptonews. Bitcoin was around $77,450 on Sunday, per The Straits Times.
items.matters: The 200-week average has marked the floor in past bear markets, so the ratio shows how close bitcoin is to that long-term support.
items.know: The tab's latest weekly close, Oct 25 2026, has bitcoin at $80,039 against a 200-week average of $67,148, a ratio of 1.19x, down from 1.31x on Oct 4. The tab counts 1.5x or lower as an 'accumulation zone', which bitcoin has been in since Jan 2026 with a low of 0.95x, though that line is illustrative and not a bottom signal. The image is the Oct 19 export, so it ends a week earlier at 1.23x and doesn't show the post-hack dip.

items.title: SpaceX revenue by segment: Space, Starlink and AI
items.picked: A post by @donaldjdean trending on X says AI is now 'what actually pays the bills' at SpaceX: AI compute brought in $7.56B of Q3's $14.6B in revenue, more than Starlink's $5.25B and Launch's $1.77B combined. SPCX closed Friday at $134.72, right at its $135 IPO price.
items.matters: SpaceX is now valued partly as an AI company, so the mix between steady Starlink revenue and fast-growing AI revenue changes how the stock trades.
items.know: For the four quarters to Sep 30 2026 the tab has Starlink at $16.023B, AI (xAI and X) $11.863B and Space $4.157B, against $11.387B, $3.201B and $4.086B for 2025. On a trailing basis Starlink is still the biggest segment, even though AI was bigger in Q3 alone. The AI numbers include the merged xAI and X businesses, and the image was redrawn from the tab because the Drive export still showed the year to June.

items.title: Starlink subscribers (millions)
items.picked: The same viral @donaldjdean post points out that Starlink went from 2.3M subscribers at the end of 2023 to 13.6M at the end of September, while SPCX trades back at its IPO price.
items.matters: Starlink is the profitable, recurring part of SpaceX, so its subscriber growth is the base that supports the heavy spending on AI.
items.know: The tab has 13.6M subscribers at Sep 2026, up from 12.0M at Jun 2026 and 8.9M at Dec 2025, so about 1.6M were added in Q3. The tab skips Sep 2025, so the points are unevenly spaced, and the count excludes several hundred thousand enterprise and aviation customers, per the company's Q3 remarks. The image was redrawn from the tab because the Drive export ended at Jun 2026.

items.title: Tesla Cybercabs on the Texas robotaxi registry
items.picked: Tesla's @robotaxi account said on Oct 30 that service now runs from 6am to 2am and claimed more than 4 million unsupervised miles, then posted a Halloween clip of a driverless Cybercab, per Where's the Driver and TeslaNorth.
items.matters: The Cybercab has no steering wheel or pedals, so how fast it shows up on the registry is the best public sign of whether Tesla can scale its purpose-built robotaxi.
items.know: The tab has 573 Cybercabs registered on Oct 31 2026, up from 544 on Oct 27, 319 on Oct 8 and 45 on Aug 31. The counts come from Texas DMV registry trackers and press reports rather than Tesla, and registered doesn't mean carrying riders. The image was redrawn from the tab because the Drive export stopped at Oct 8.

items.title: AI payback gap: cloud revenue vs capex at Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft (TTM)
items.picked: Alphabet fell about 13% on Oct 29, its worst day ever, and Microsoft's quarterly capex of $45.2B came in below the $50.67B estimate as it trimmed its full-year outlook, per CNBC. Neocloud stocks fell after the Microsoft numbers.
items.matters: This chart asks the core AI question: how much cloud revenue the three biggest clouds get for each dollar they spend on capex.
items.know: In the four quarters to Jun 2026 the tab has $440.42B of cloud revenue against $421.38B of capex, or $1.05 of cloud revenue per $1 of capex, down from $2.07 in Dec 2023. Capex has more than tripled since then while cloud revenue rose about 77%. The tab ends with the Jun quarter, so it doesn't include the Sep-quarter results reported this week, and capex covers the whole company, not only cloud.

items.title: What the bond market expects from the Fed: 2-year Treasury yield minus fed funds
items.picked: The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on Oct 28, and bond traders saw about a 90% chance of a December hike right afterward, per Moneycontrol. The October jobs report is due Friday, Nov 6.
items.matters: When the 2-year yield sits well above the fed funds rate, the bond market is betting the Fed's next move is a hike, which hurts high-valuation stocks like AI names.
items.know: The tab has the gap at 0.89 points for Oct 2026 and 1.00 for Sep 2026, the highest since Oct 2022 (1.43), when the Fed was hiking fast. It was -0.42 in Nov 2025, when markets expected cuts. The data is month-end, and the image is the Oct 19 export, so its October point may not match the final 0.89.
